The FOMC statement projects a supportive macro backdrop—solid job gains, low unemployment, inflation near 2 percent, and a transitory Q1 growth slowdown—with an accommodative policy stance and balanced near-term risks.

Incorporating the April 2017 SLOOS nudges that optimism down a notch. The survey points to mixed credit conditions: domestic banks reported tightening for auto loans and greater caution in CRE lending; foreign banks raised loan rates and interest rate floors and lowered loan-to-value ratios, indicating stricter terms. Offsetting this somewhat, banks eased on credit card lending and maintained willingness to extend consumer installment loans. On net, SLOOS suggests slightly tighter financial intermediation than implied by the FOMC’s tone, warranting a modestly more cautious read.
